blog.title: Free Family Scam-Safety Kit: pages to keep by the phone
blog.meta: Six free printables for families, word for word: a callback card, a family safe word, house rules for AI, and what to do if a scam gets through.

sections.heading: A family safe word
sections.text:
Scammers can now copy a voice from a short clip, such as a video posted online. A call can sound exactly like your grandson or your daughter. A safe word is a word only your family knows. If a caller cannot say it, it is not your family.

- **Easy to remember**, even when you are upset.
- **Hard to guess.** Not a pet's name, a street, a birthday, a team, or anything posted online.
- **A little odd.** Two words that do not usually go together work well. A made-up example: "blue teapot." Do not use that one.
- **The same for everyone** who might call for help or get the call.

- Share it **in person** only.
- Do not text it, email it, post it, or type it into any AI.
- Do not say it where a smart speaker or a video call could pick it up.
- If you think someone outside the family has heard it, choose a new one.

1. A caller says they are family and need help or money.
2. You ask: "What's our word?"
3. If they cannot say it, hang up. Call back on a number you already know.
4. Even if they say it, you can still hang up and call back. That is always allowed.

A real family member will never be upset that you checked.
sections.source: Products/AI for Every Age/free-kit/2 - Family safe-word guide.md

sections.heading: House rules for AI
sections.text:
- **No secrets go into AI.** No passwords, account numbers, Social Security numbers, medical records, or children's names, photos or schools.
- **An adult is present.** Children do not use AI on their own. If a child has an idea for an AI, they tell an adult, and the adult types it in their own words.
- **AI is a helper, not a friend.** We talk about worries and problems with people, not with a chatbot.
- **We check before we trust.** AI can sound sure and still be wrong. We check facts with a real source.
- **We call back before we pay.** Any call or message asking for money gets a callback on a number we already know.
sections.source: Products/AI for Every Age/free-kit/3 - Family AI Agreement.md

sections.heading: What never goes into an AI
sections.text:
1. **Social Security numbers** (and Medicare, passport and driver's license numbers)
2. **Account numbers:** bank, card, loan, policy
3. **Passwords,** and the codes texted to your phone
4. **Medical records**
5. **Children's names, photos and schools**
When in doubt, leave it out.

- I swapped names for labels like [MY NAME] or [DOCTOR].
- I deleted addresses the task does not need.
- I removed every ID, account and card number.
- I removed passwords and codes.
- For a photo: I covered private parts with a sticky note, and checked the photo before sending.
If I cannot remove the private details, I do not paste it. I ask a person I trust instead.
sections.source: Products/AI for Every Age/free-kit/4 - Never-paste list.md

sections.heading: A message you did not expect
sections.text:
Use this for any call, text, email or message you did not expect. Start at the top. One "yes" is enough to stop.

1. Does it ask for money, a gift card, cryptocurrency or a wire transfer? Yes → STOP.
2. Does it ask for a password, a code sent to your phone, or an account, card or Social Security number? Yes → STOP. No real company or relative needs these from you by phone or message.
3. Does it rush you? "Today." "Right now." "Or your account closes." Yes → STOP.
4. Does it ask you to keep it secret? "Don't tell your bank." "Don't tell Mom." Yes → STOP.
5. Does it want you to tap a link, open a file, or call a number it gave you? Yes → Don't. Go to the company's own app or website, or call a number you already know.
sections.source: Products/AI for Every Age/free-kit/6 - Scam decision tree.md

sections.heading: If a scam gets through
sections.text:
It is not your fault. Act fast. In this order:

1. **Stop.** Do not send more money, even if they threaten you.
2. **Call your bank** on the number on the back of your card. Ask them to stop or reverse the payment.
3. **Tell someone you trust.**
4. **Report it to the FTC:** ReportFraud.ftc.gov
5. **Report it to the FBI:** ic3.gov
6. **Need help reporting? Age 60 or over?** Elder Fraud Hotline: (833) 372-8311, Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern.
7. **Freeze your credit** with all three bureaus. It is free. Equifax · Experian · TransUnion
8. **Identity stolen?** IdentityTheft.gov
9. **Write it down:** dates, amounts, names, numbers, what was said.

Anyone who offers to "recover" your money for a fee is almost always another scammer.
sections.source: Products/AI for Every Age/free-kit/5 - If it happens card.md
